title: phase-bj: mechanical close flow: close hook, stack bead, sanity-stack, runs tabs
description:
Repository: randlee/atm-bd-orchestration. Code, worktrees, sprint branches and PRs live there, on its `integrate/phase-bj`; atm-core's `integrate/phase-bj` holds only this plan. The rulings are Rand's of 2026-10-18, anchored as ANC-051..088 in `docs/plans/phase-bj/anchors.md` (ANC-062 retired by ANC-065); the requirement docs are `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` of atm-bd-orchestration PR #342 with the dev, dev-sanity, team-lead and quality-mgr requirement items they amend.

## Goal
Dev work is not complete until sanity verifies it, and the lead does not need to intervene between a dev push and the QA assignment:
- one script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes; it checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead (ANC-051..059, ANC-070);
- the dev's ATM task stays open until the sanity close hook closes it on PASS; a sanity FAIL is one `sanity-fail.xml.j2` message to the dev on that open task, no finding children, counted in `metadata.sanity_round` up to `max_sanity_rounds` (default 5) (ANC-055..057, ANC-072);
- the stack bead `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack` is the ledger and the lock of the phase stack; the sanity side links the layer on PASS under its claim, first PASS wins the top and the other dev gets `rebase-required` without a round counted; a sanity-stack subagent handles one next-top layer per spawn, sequentially, with a lean mode and a lock timeout that never blocks the team and never escalates to a person (ANC-065..069, ANC-071);
- the pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty onto every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead and validates the projected phase graph before writes (ANC-083, atm-bd-orchestration #340);
- `atm-bd console` shows a sanity runs tab and a quality runs tab, newest first, QA run-level verdict and elapsed, the dev's name and icon, and an API_FAILURE kind distinct from a FAIL verdict (ANC-073, atm-bd-orchestration #347).

Dev and fix assignment stay the lead's (ANC-060); atm-bd assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task (ANC-061).

No per-reviewer quality metadata is promised: the producer is outside phase-bj, so the quality tab displays only fields and findings already written by in-scope producers.

## Sprints

| bj-1 | close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds | root | - |
| bj-2 | stack bead and sprint-family pour: stack-bead.json.j2, pour metadata, pydantic model per bead kind, validate-plan | root | - |
| bj-3 | sanity-stack subagent and dev-sanity PASS wiring: sequential spawns, lock timeout, lean mode | must_follow | bj-1, bj-2 |
| bj-4 | console sanity and quality runs tabs; measured elapsed and dev identity in the sanity ledger | parallel_safe | - |
| bj-5 | out-of-band full-skill integrity manifest; install verification and hand-runnable plugin doctor | parallel_safe | - |

`requirements` and `adrs` are `NONE` on every sprint: the atm-core requirement and ADR documents do not govern atm-bd-orchestration code; the governing text is the package's `docs/requirements/*.md` named per sprint.

## BJ5 integrity addition (atm-bd-orchestration #349)
`bj-5` publishes an out-of-band sc-sha manifest for all shipped skill files, verifies files against the selected release manifest during `atm-bd skill` install, and ships a hand-runnable plugin doctor reporting per-file status and aggregate PASS/FAIL. It hashes with the `sc-sha` package's `sc_sha` module, stores no SHA inside any file, leaves sc-publish unchanged, and has no dependency on atm-core. Anchors: ANC-087, ANC-088. requirements/adrs: NONE.

## Decisions
- The hook is a script the agent runs as the last step of its template.
- The stack bead is poured with the phase root from a template, never created by hand; `validate-plan` requires it (team-lead 13).
- The sanity side links; the lead never links. The lead owns unstack, sync, rebase, merge and every `stack_failed`, always under the stack bead claim (team-lead 42).
- Nothing is a new process artifact: no class beads, outage beads, holds, refusal citations or checker-defect channel (ANC-084..086); the sanity run table template is retired by the runs tab.

## Success Criteria
- A dev bead closed through `atm-task-close.py --role dev` in a scratch repository leaves the dev's ATM task open, closes the bead, and assigns the sanity task as the phase lead with no lead action (ANC-052, ANC-055).
- A sanity PASS through the hook closes the dev's task as the lead and assigns QA as the lead; a sanity FAIL sends one `sanity-fail` message on the dev's open task and creates no bead (ANC-053, ANC-056, ANC-072).
- Two branches cut from the same top that both pass sanity: the first advances the stack bead from empty to singleton against trunk, the second is linked as the hosted top in `layers`; a conflicting second branch gets `rebase-required` and `sanity_round` does not move (ANC-065, ANC-067, ANC-071).
- `validate-plan --phase bj` requires the stack bead and every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead carries branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty (ANC-083).
- `atm-bd console` shows the sanity and quality tabs with run-level QA verdict and elapsed, the dev's icon and name, and an API_FAILURE icon distinct from FAIL (ANC-073).
- Every sprint's QA PASS at its head; the stack lands on `integrate/phase-bj` of atm-bd-orchestration; `just lint` and `just test` green there.
- `atm-bd skill` verifies every installed file against the selected release manifest and refuses mismatches with the path list; `atm-hook-doctor.py` reports per-file integrity and aggregate PASS/FAIL from the install-recorded manifest, hashing only with the `sc-sha` package's `sc_sha` module (ANC-087, ANC-088).
- Phase BJ5 uses no atm-core dependency, embeds no SHA in shipped files, and leaves sc-publish unchanged.

title: bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds
description:
## Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 070, 071, 072.

## Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). No template names `--skip-checks`.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47).
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `--skip-checks` absent from every template and agent file; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing.

## Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` before coding; the command sequences there are the specification.
- `sc_render.render` for every template render, strict; never pipe a render into `jq`.
- Every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, in the fixed shape above.
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

## Replay Safety
Every hook write boundary is replay-safe using the existing bead and ATM task events; no second ledger is introduced. Before each write, inspect bead metadata/events and ATM task state; if the intended same verdict/head write is already recorded, skip it, and reject a conflicting verdict or head with a typed error. A report/assignment is keyed by the role task id and verdict/head; replay may re-notify via a same-id assignment update (atm-core #1619) but may not create a second task. Injected-runner failure tests cover each boundary, including close, report, counter update, dev reopen, sanity reset/close, dev-task close and QA assignment; replay neither double-counts FAIL nor double-sends a new task, and eventually completes. The FAIL counter increments once per distinct verdict event. The close/report/assignment command ordering is explicit and any interruption resumes from recorded state. A not_reproducible fix strict-renders the report and sanity assignment using the same vars path without commit, PR number or branch.

## Public Contract
```
atm-task-close.py --role dev|fix|sanity|qa --vars <file> [--skip-checks]
stdout: {"ok": {"role": ..., "bead": ..., "commit": ..., "pr_number": ..., "github": "ok"|"unavailable", "assigned": [<task ids>], "closed": [<bead ids>]}}
      | {"err": {"code": "VARS.MISSING"|"VARS.EMPTY"|"HEAD.NOT_PUSHED"|"BASE.NOT_ANCESTOR"|"PR.NOT_FOUND"|"PR.BASE"|"SANITY.NOT_STACKED"|"SANITY.ROUND_CAP"|"BEAD.NO_SANITY", "message": ..., "fix": ...}}
exit 0 on ok, 1 on err
```
Identity per command (task-close-hook.md 4):
```python
LEAD_ENV = {**os.environ, "ATM_IDENTITY": lead, "ATM_TEAM": team}   # atm task assign; atm task close <checked bead>
run(["atm", "task", "assign", member, "--task-id", bead, "--template", tpl, "--vars", vars_path], env=LEAD_ENV)
run(["bd", "close", bead, "--reason", reason, "--actor", os.environ["ATM_IDENTITY"]])        # caller
```
`task-close-vars.j2` header:
```
---
name: task-close-vars
format: text
required_variables are selected by role and outcome from one shared vars contract: `role`, `phase`, `sprint`, distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, `qa_bead`, `branch`, `worktree_path`, `pr_target`, `base`, `lint_command`, `primary_checkout`, `report_inventory`, `commit`, `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `round`, `verdict`, `outcome`, `reviewer`, `policy`, `carry_forward`, `evidence`. Required/nonempty matrix: dev completion requires dev id, branch/worktree/pr_target/base/lint/checkout/report/commit/pr fields; fixed fix completion same; not_reproducible fix requires fix id, outcome, evidence and report inventory only (no commit/PR/branch); sanity assignment requires sanity id, checked bead and verdict/round; QA assignment requires QA id/bead, base, commit, round, reviewer/policy; completion reports require their own role id and report/status fields. No role-inapplicable field is required or defaulted empty.
---
```
Ancestor check: read StackMetadata, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<layers[-1].branch> HEAD`; use `origin/<pr_target>` only when layers is empty. The PR check: `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls?head=<o>:<branch>&state=open` filtered to number, base.ref, head.sha.

Strict end-to-end renders use the exact same vars file at every dev, sanity and QA send/assignment; each destination body names the id passed by `--task-id`.

Also owned: the four completion templates, `assignment-gates.py` and its tests, and tests for the deleted sanity-create-findings script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (ANC-054) `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity; the source reads only the last stack layer (or pr_target for an empty ledger) and contains no lint or test subprocess.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id.
- [ ] (ANC-057) five distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting leave `sanity_round` at 5, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the fifth, the sanity bead `in_progress` assigned to the lead, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to the lead; replaying the fifth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the second run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward`, the round's filing reviewer; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; the operational invocation scan finds no `--skip-checks` use in templates/agents; a separate help test verifies the script documents the option.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (ANC-071) `rg -n sanity_round scripts/atm-task-close.py` shows the only increment on the FAIL branch.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` does not exist and nothing references it: script and its two tests are absent; the manifest has one bj-3 owner for inventory cleanup, and composed installed-skill validation after bj-3 reports no active reference (historical changelog excluded).
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; `rg -n "atm task close .* completed" templates/dev-template.xml.j2 templates/fix-assignment.xml.j2` returns nothing.

title: bj-3: sanity-stack subagent and dev-sanity PASS wiring: sequential spawns, lock timeout, lean mode
description:
## Goal
On a sanity PASS the sanity side links the checked PR as the new top of the phase stack under the stack bead's claim before the close hook runs; when more than one sanity task is open, or its own inline link failed, dev-sanity spawns the `sanity-stack` subagent, one spawn at a time in verdict order, each handling exactly one next-top layer. The race is the subagent's job: first PASS wins the top, the other dev gets `rebase-required` with no round counted; a lock timeout returns the holder and never blocks the team or escalates to a person. Governing text: `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` 1 to 13, `dev-sanity.md` 9, 10, 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, `team-lead.md` 22, 42, 43. Anchors: ANC-065, 066, 067, 068, 069, 071, 074.

## Prerequisites (what this sprint consumes)
- bj-1 delivers `atm-task-close.py --role sanity`, which refuses a PASS close without a stack result in the vars (`stacked` with the new top and `stack_number`) and sends `rebase-required.xml.j2`; this sprint's procedures end by running that hook with that result (ANC-055, ANC-065).
- bj-2 delivers the stack bead `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack` with `metadata.trunk`, `stack_number` and `layers` of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` validated by `bead_schema.py`; this sprint writes `layers` under the bead's claim (ANC-067).

## Deliverables
1. `agents/sanity-stack.md`: a subagent of dev-sanity (tools Bash, Read), one next-top layer per spawn. Input, one fenced JSON object: `checked_bead`, `branch`, `pr_number`, `commit`, `stack_bead`, `budget` (`full` or `lean`), `timeout_s` (default 60). Procedure: claim the stack bead with `bd update <stack bead> --claim`, retrying every 5 s until `timeout_s`; under the lock and in this order with nothing between: re-read `layers` from the bead (never from the input), `git fetch origin`, choose the current top branch or `trunk` when the ledger is empty, then verify that baseline is an ancestor of `commit`; `full`: link every `linked: false` layer in order then this PR as the new top (`gh stack link <stack_number> <pr>`; the first stack from layers 0 and 1 with `--base <trunk>`), one `/sc-gh-stack-view`; `lean`: the ancestor check above is the only divergence check; append the first empty-ledger PASS as a singleton with base trunk, and preserve all unlinked entries during later catch-up; verify the PR base ref equals the top branch from one filtered REST pull list (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls?state=open&per_page=100 --jq` to number, base, head, sha, draft; never the raw body) and record `linked: false`; append the layer; write the metadata with `bd update --metadata @file.json`; release with `bd update <stack bead> --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --status open --assignee ""`. Output, one fenced JSON object: `stacked` (new top, nullable `stack_number` for an initial singleton), `rebase_required`, `lock_timeout` (holder, claim time, holder's active task from `atm task list`) or `stack_failed`, with the evidence. GraphQL unavailable is detected and forces `lean`; a lean run makes no GraphQL call (ANC-069). Ancestor check fails: `rebase_required`, link nothing, write nothing (ANC-065). A link that fails for a stack reason is repaired with the `sc-gh-stack` recipes within this one layer, never rewriting a layer with children; unrecoverable: `stack_failed`, lock released, ledger unchanged. Under the lock, reconcile the hosted chain against existing ledger entries without replacing the ledger: preserve every `linked:false` entry; mark only proven links as linked; record hosted-only partial results only when uniquely attributable; ambiguity or conflicting ancestry returns `stack_failed` without ledger mutation. There is no automatic reclaim: a claim still held at `timeout_s` returns `lock_timeout`, and only the lead releases a stuck claim, by hand. The metadata commit and the release are both `bd update <stack bead> --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY"`; a mismatch (exit 13) leaves the ledger unchanged. dev-sanity waits for each spawn's result before the next, so no second writer of the same identity exists; never call `bd reclaim` or infer lease expiry from bead event age. The agent never refuses the task, never sends the dev a FAIL, never escalates to a person (ANC-068).
2. `agents/dev-sanity.md` PASS path (dev-sanity 28, sanity-stack.md 12, 13): one sanity task open: dev-sanity runs the procedure of deliverable 1 itself, inline, same order, same lock; more than one open, or its own inline link failed: it spawns `sanity-stack`, one spawn at a time in verdict order, never two in flight (ANC-066). `stacked`: run `atm-task-close.py --role sanity` with the stack result in the vars. A `not_reproducible` fix has no new PR: dev-sanity verifies the cited `file:line` at the commit and branch the assignment names (the current stack top, deliverable 4 of bj-1), spawns no `sanity-stack`, links nothing, and closes PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result. `rebase_required`: reopen the checked bead to the dev, send `rebase-required.xml.j2` on the dev's open task, leave `sanity_round` unchanged, keep the PASS in the ledger, close nothing (ANC-071). `lock_timeout`: keep the sanity task active, send the holder one plain message asking for the release, continue other sanity checks, re-spawn after the holder's reply or after another `timeout_s`; never refuse, never FAIL the dev, never a person (ANC-068). `stack_failed`: report to the lead as stack owner with the evidence and keep the task active (team-lead 22). `budget` is `lean` when GraphQL is unavailable or the agent is watching its token budget.
3. `agents/dev-sanity.md` items 9 and 10 (ANC-084..086): the dev-sanity coordinator makes one Jev client call and does not add a second retry loop; the bj-4-owned Jev client defines and tests its bounded transport retry policy; an oversized context is shortened and the call retried by that client, never returned to dev-sanity as a failure; the failure reason is the verbatim error, kept in the run's ledger row as kind `API_FAILURE`, never a FAIL verdict; every fallback use is logged with its verbatim error and said once in the close report. The LLM subagent spawn is fenced by a start and end timer whose elapsed is written as `llm_elapsed_s` to the ledger row. No class bead, outage bead, hold on re-dispatch, refusal citation or checker-defect side channel appears anywhere in the agent text.
4. `manifest.yaml` ships `agents/sanity-stack.md`; `install.py` copies it like the other agents without a code change. The generated block is written only by `tests/gen_manifest.py`, never by hand; bj-5 runs the same generator for its files, and the later of the two layers regenerates it at rebase so `gen_manifest.py --check` passes on the stack top.
5. `CHANGELOG.md`: the phase entry for bj-1, bj-2 and bj-3 (close hook, stack bead and pour, sanity-stack), written here because this sprint lands after both.
6. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_agent_prompts.py`: the agent files contain the required phrases and none of the forbidden ones: `rg -n "class bead|outage bead|hold on re-dispatch|citation|checker-defect" agents` returns nothing; `sanity-stack.md` names `timeout_s`, `budget`, `lock_timeout`, `rebase_required`, `stack_failed`, `--claim`, `--if-assignee`; `dev-sanity.md` forbids a second spawn while one is in flight.

## Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` first; the procedure order under the lock is normative.
- Prompt text is minimal: a procedure, not an essay; measured facts only (a REST pull list of 100 PRs filtered to five fields is about 3 KB).

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- The hook itself and the templates (bj-1); the stack bead schema and pour (bj-2); the console tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).
- The lead's stack recipes (unstack, restack, land under the claim): the `sc-gh-stack` skill and `team-lead.md` 42 already state them; no script is added.

## Recovery and Retry
Recovery is driven by injected clock and command responses. It preserves ledger-only unlinked lean entries, reconciles only uniquely attributable hosted link events, and fails closed on ambiguity. Every metadata commit is guarded by `--if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY"`; there is no automatic reclaim. Jev retries are owned by bj-4 at the actual HTTP client boundary; dev-sanity makes one call and records the returned API_FAILURE without coordinator retry multiplication.

## Goal
For atm-bd-orchestration issue #349: atm-bd's built wheel and sdist carry a manifest of every shipped skill file's sc-sha; `atm-bd skill` verifies the files it installs against that published manifest; a hand-runnable plugin doctor checks an installed copy without atm-core. This is phase-bj work in atm-bd-orchestration, independent of bj-1 through bj-4. Anchors: ANC-087, ANC-088, ANC-003, ANC-010, ANC-011, ANC-012. No SHA is written into any source file; hashing is the `sc-sha` package's `sc_sha` module; the sc-publish kit (`.github/scripts`, `.github/actions`) is unchanged.

## Deliverables
1. `apps/atm-bd-console/hatch_build.py`: in `_include_skills`, after choosing the bundled skill tree, write `skill-manifest.json` (schema version, atm-bd version, one `{path, sc_sha}` per shipped file of the plugin tree in sorted path order, and `sc_sha.calculate_composition_hash` over them) into the build output and force-include it beside the bundled skills in both the wheel and the sdist. This is the published manifest: it exists only in the built artifacts that sc-publish uploads, never in git.
2. `apps/atm-bd-console/pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`: add `sc-sha>=1.7.0,<2` to the runtime dependencies and to the build-system requires, so `import sc_sha` works in the build and in an installed atm-bd. `sc_sha.calculate_hash` is the per-file hash; no other hasher is written.
3. `apps/atm-bd-console/src/atm_bd_console/skill_integrity.py` (new): `load_manifest(source)`, `verify_tree(pkg_dir, manifest) -> list[PathResult]` with `ok|modified|missing|extra`, and `write_install_record(dest, version, commit, manifest, installed)`. Sources of the published manifest: bare `atm-bd skill` reads the one packaged in the installed wheel (no network, ANC-010); `atm-bd skill x.y.z` reads the manifest from the published atm-bd x.y.z sdist on PyPI (`https://pypi.org/pypi/atm-bd/<x.y.z>/json`), and `--latest` does the same for the newest published version on PyPI, whose tag `v<version>` it installs (ANC-012 v3).
4. `apps/atm-bd-console/src/atm_bd_console/skill_source.py`: `--latest` resolves the newest published version on PyPI and clones its `v<version>` tag instead of `main`; bare keeps the packaged files (ANC-010) and `x.y.z` keeps cloning the `vX.Y.Z` tag of atm-bd-orchestration (ANC-011).
5. `apps/atm-bd-console/src/atm_bd_console/skill.py`: inside the existing `with skill_source.resolve_source(...)` block, call `verify_tree(source.pkg_dir, manifest)` before `installer.plan_install`; any `modified` or `missing` path stops the install before any write, prints one `<status> <path>` line per path and returns exit 1. After `installer.apply_plan`, call `write_install_record` with the version, commit and the sc-sha of each file as installed (rendered team, prefix and member values make installed bytes differ from published bytes by design). The `installed ... from <ref> @ <commit> (atm-bd <version>)` line is unchanged (ANC-003). The plugin `install.py` (bj-1's fence) is called as today and not edited.
6. `plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/atm-hook-doctor.py` (new): reads the install record in the target `.claude` (or `.codex`) directory, hashes each recorded installed file with `sc_sha.calculate_hash`, prints one `ok|modified|missing|extra` line per path and `PASS` or `FAIL`; exposes the same check as `doctor(dest) -> Result` for phase-bk's `hook.doctor()`. It imports nothing from atm-core or atm_bd_console; when `sc_sha` is missing it exits 2 with the fix `uv pip install 'sc-sha>=1.7.0,<2'`.
7. `manifest.yaml`: regenerate its generated block with `tests/gen_manifest.py` so the doctor script ships; this sprint never hand-edits the block (Ownership below).

Tests (deterministic fixture trees, controlled file contents, injected PyPI/git responses, no sleeps): manifest coverage and aggregate, verification pass and refusal for bare, `x.y.z` and `--latest`, install-record contents, doctor outcomes, and the built wheel and sdist each containing `skill-manifest.json`.

## Ownership
`manifest.yaml`'s artifact block is generated by `tests/gen_manifest.py` from the files present. bj-3 and bj-5 both add shipped files, so each regenerates the block in its own layer and never hand-edits it; at the later layer's rebase the block is regenerated again, which is the conflict resolution. design:
## Public Contract
Published manifest: `skill-manifest.json` inside the atm-bd wheel and sdist, written by the build hook at build time: `{schema: 1, version, files: [{path, sc_sha}], aggregate}`. Paths are relative to the plugin root and sorted; `aggregate` is `sc_sha.calculate_composition_hash` over the sorted list.

`atm-bd skill` (bare, `x.y.z`, `--latest`) verifies every file of the resolved tree against the manifest of the release it installs before calling the installer; mismatch = exit 1, one `modified <path>` or `missing <path>` line each, nothing written. Install record `<dest>/atm-bd-install.json`: `{version, commit, source, files: [{path, sc_sha}]}` with installed-file hashes.

`atm-hook-doctor.py [--dest <dir>]`: per-path `ok|modified|missing|extra`, aggregate `PASS|FAIL`, exit 0/1; the same function is `doctor(dest)`.

## Exact Targets
See owned_paths. `install.py`, `.github/**` and every bj-1..bj-4 file are untouched.
